body:
Findings-round grading: **held** (`finding` stays; routing deliberately left blank).

- **Stale-premise check on `origin/main` @ `e5bd768`**: both sets verified live and still divergent by exactly `code` — `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts:36` (`NAME_LIKE_FIELDS` includes `'code'`) vs `packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts:134-136` (`NAME_ISH_EXACT` does not). The skill doc still teaches the lint spelling.
- **Why held**: whether the two sets are *meant* to be one set is ADR-0079's recorded open question 4 — the #6634 reconstruction was explicitly not allowed to invent that decision, and neither is triage. Nothing is user-visible today (R9 is `severity: 'suggestion'`; the `Record #(id)` floor guarantees a title regardless), so there is no defect to queue ahead of the ruling.
- **Routing left blank deliberately**: the fix lands in `packages/lint` (`domain:devx`) or `packages/spec/src/data` (`domain:spec`) depending on which set is judged authoritative — routing would presuppose the answer.
- **Restart condition**: a ruling on ADR-0079 open question 4, or either set being edited again (which would force the question).

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

The one-entry divergence (`code`) is real but its resolution is recorded as ADR-0079 open question 4 — the right moment to settle it is an ADR-0079 open-questions ruling round, not a standalone micro-card that would pre-empt the ADR's own process. Restart condition: ADR-0079's open questions get ruled (escalate this card into that batch), or a user-visible mis-derivation on a `code`-only object is reported (then it promotes on its own evidence).

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-10, directed in session `session_01BPWqbmEFU8gJepBJTHESXd`): document the gap, no behavior change.**

The two "name-like" sets (lint R9's title faces, spec's ADR-0079 derivation keys) stay as they are; the undocumented difference — `code` counting for one and not the other — gets written down where both sets are defined, each pointing at the other. R9 is suggestion-severity, so the stakes do not justify moving either set; the defect was that the divergence was invisible, not that it exists.

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` (docs-note card).

**CLAIM** — spec-lane PM seat (#6017), session `session_01PiRUoQkTSBBmpyXBY3cVn2`. Branch: `claude/issue-6734-name-like-sets-note`. Dispatching a **cloud dev session** (model: Opus — smallest card of the batch; a docs-note whose one trap is the ADR boundary).

Executing the maintainer's 2026-08-10 ruling (comment 5237222790): **document the gap, no behavior change.** Both sets stay exactly as they are. The divergence — `code` in lint R9's `NAME_LIKE_FIELDS` (`packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts:36`) but not in spec's `NAME_ISH_EXACT` (`packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts`) — gets written down **where both sets are defined, each pointing at the other**, stating that R9 asks the looser "will records be anonymous?" question while ADR-0079 derivation asks "what is the title?", and that the one-entry difference is intentional. Also update `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:1091` (re-anchor by content), which currently teaches the lint set as the contract — add the same distinction note there so the drift stops being taught.

⛔ **Do NOT touch `docs/adr/**`** — ADR-0079 records this as its open question 4, and resolving that entry is a maintainer-merged ADR edit (PD #14). State in the PR body that the ADR's open-question ledger can be updated by the maintainer separately, and leave the file alone. No behavior change means **zero** test/output movement: `git diff` must contain comments, docs and SKILL.md prose only; if any code path would move, STOP. Changeset: none expected for comment-only source edits — follow the repo's skip-changeset convention for docs-only diffs and justify whichever applies.
